entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: No representation from the petitioner.

Notice was already issued to the petitioner intimating the adjournment of the case, and also informing him that the case would be decided in his absence, if there is no representation on the adjourned posting date.
Still, the petitioner did not opt to appear before this Court, or make necessary arrangements for advancing arguments.

2. The order under challenge in this revision petition is one passed by the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Kannur, on 23.01.2007, dismissing the petition filed by the petitioner under Section 20A of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,1954.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Kannur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In the aforesaid case, which was numbered as STC No.808/2004, the petitioner was facing criminal prosecution for the commission of offence under Sections 16(1)(a)(i) of the aforesaid Act.
He filed C.M.P.No.426/2007 stating that the Commission Agent, who supplied the misbranded food items, should also be impleaded as an accused in that case.

3. The application was opposed by the prosecution contending that the document relied on by the petitioner in support of the above 2026:KER:26770        3 plea, was only a delivery note,
which is not sufficient for invoking the powers under Section 20A of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,1954, for impleadment of the persons referred thereunder.
The learned Magistrate accepted the aforesaid contention of the prosecution, and dismissed the petition filed by the petitioner.
On going through the reasoning adopted by the learned Magistrate, I am of the view that there is absolutely no reason for interference, in exercise of the revisional powers of this Court.
Accordingly, I find this revision petition devoid of merits.
In the result, the petition is hereby dismissed.
